dialect.detail: Likely compiled with a Unix/Linux COBOL compiler (possibly MicroFocus or similar); references to .slr copybooks, socket program interface (cpi5.c), and 78-level constants suggest COBOL-85 or later. Developed by 'dyad infoSys' for a medical practice management system.

purpose.domain_detail: Patient master file management for a regional medical associates practice management system; handles patient lookup, add, and update operations including MRN, OHIP numbers, chart numbers, and eligibility history.
purpose.summary: This program (cpirma5) is a COBOL batch/subprogram called from a C socket program (cpi5.c) that manages patient master records for a medical practice. It supports lookup, add, and update of patient demographics including health card numbers, chart numbers, birth dates, and eligibility history across multiple indexed files. It also produces audit and error reports.

notable_features: 21 COPY statements for file control and data definitions (.slr/.fd/.ws extensions)
Multiple indexed file access with alternate keys (surname+givenname index)
Called from C socket program (cpi5.c) via linkage section buffer
Province table with Canadian provinces (OHIP/Ontario health context)
Y2K fix noted in comments (4-digit birth year)
No COMP-3 usage despite financial/medical context
verdict.notes: Source truncated to first 16000 chars; full program is 1677 lines. Canadian medical practice management system (OHIP = Ontario Health Insurance Plan). Developed by 'dyad infoSys', written 2002-2003. The .slr copybook extension and socket interface suggest a Unix/Linux environment. No EXEC CICS or EXEC SQL. Dialect family is uncertain between MicroFocus and other Unix COBOL compilers.
